data.title: Smithfield Foods Supports Students Through Feed the Children Resource Rallies
data.description:
Partnership includes a $100,000 contribution and protein donations from Smithfield to help 1,200 families prepare for the school year

SMITHFIELD, Va., Aug. 07, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Smithfield Foods and Feed the Children, a global movement working to end childhood hunger, launched a series of three Feed the Children Resource Rallies today to help families prepare for the upcoming school year.

“Every child deserves the opportunity to learn, grow and reach their full potential,” said Jim Monroe, vice president, corporate affairs for Smithfield Foods. “Through our partnership with Feed the Children, we're helping students enter the classroom with the tools and confidence they need to succeed.”

The series of Feed the Children Resource Rallies began today in Nashville, Tennessee, one of three communities within Smithfield’s broader operational footprint. Additional rallies are planned in Denison, Iowa, on Aug. 12 and Kinston, North Carolina, on Aug. 19. Each rally will support approximately 400 families by providing food, essentials and school supplies.

Smithfield is contributing $100,000 and providing thousands of pounds of protein, including ham, bacon and lunchmeat, for families attending the Resource Rallies. Local Smithfield employees will volunteer their time alongside community partners to help make the events possible.

“Back-to-school season should be a time of hope and possibility, but for too many families working hard to provide for their children, it also brings real hunger and hardship,” said Emily Callahan, president and CEO of Feed the Children. “Together with Smithfield Foods, we’re helping ease that burden by putting food, essentials and school supplies directly into the hands of families who need them most. That’s what our global movement is about — ensuring every child has the resources they need to survive and thrive.”

Participating families will receive a 25-pound box of shelf-stable food including items such as canned vegetables, beans, soup, pasta, cereal and peanut butter. They will also receive a 15-pound box of essential hygiene items including shampoo, laundry detergent, razors and toothpaste. In addition, children will be given backpacks filled with school supplies, personal care items and a shelf-stable meal kit.

The 2026 Feed the Children Resource Rallies build on a three-year partnership between Smithfield and Feed the Children focused on providing families with food, household essentials and school supplies so students are better prepared for success in the classroom.

Since 2008, Smithfield has donated more than 340 million servings of protein to fight hunger and address food insecurity through the company’s Helping Hungry Homes® program. To learn more about Smithfield’s initiatives to strengthen local communities, visit smithfieldfoods.com/good-is-what-we-do.

About Smithfield Foods

Smithfield Foods is an American food company with a leading position in packaged meats and fresh pork products. With a diverse brand portfolio and strong relationships with U.S. farmers and customers, we responsibly meet demand for quality protein around the world.

About Feed the Children

Feed the Children is a global movement working to end childhood hunger in the U.S. and around the world. Together with communities, the organization provides food, essentials and opportunities to children and families who need them most so every child can survive and thrive. Learn more at feedthechildren.org.

Feed the Children | Create a world where no child goes to bed hungry

data.title: NB Bancorp, Inc. Q2 2026: Revenue $111.8M, Net income $21.1M, EPS $0.53— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
NB Bancorp, Inc. reported second-quarter 2026 results with revenue of $111.8M, net income of $21.1M and diluted EPS of $0.53, all materially higher versus the year‑ago quarter as loan growth and higher interest‑earning assets drove earnings.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $111.8M for Q2 2026, compared with $79.8M in the year‑ago quarter; YoY change 40.0%.
  • Net income was $21.1M for Q2 2026, compared with $14.6M in the year‑ago quarter; YoY change 44.9%.
  • Diluted EPS was $0.53 for Q2 2026, compared with $0.39 in the year‑ago quarter; YoY change 35.9%.

Business Highlights

  • Revenue growth was driven by net interest income, which surged roughly 47% quarter‑over‑quarter (Q2) and about 48% year‑to‑date, reflecting loan portfolio expansion and a larger base of interest‑earning assets.
  • Loan balances increased about 7.5% versus year‑end, led by commercial, commercial real estate, C&I, multi‑family and cannabis lending.
  • Management shifted channel and product mix toward higher‑yield, shorter‑term loans and emphasized growth in core deposits (noninterest demand & NOW) to manage interest rate risk.
  • Operational investments tied to the integration of Provident and technology upgrades raised headcount, data processing, branch openings and operating expenses as the company scales.
  • Fee and other noninterest income rose roughly 30% in Q2, supported by higher cash management activity and transaction volumes.

Original SEC Filing: NB Bancorp, Inc. [ NBBK ] - 10-Q - Aug. 07, 2026

data.title: Heritage Insurance Holdings 2Q 2026: Revenue $214.2M, EPS $2.05— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Heritage Insurance Holdings reported second-quarter 2026 results with revenue of $214.2M and diluted EPS of $2.05, as net income attributable to common stockholders rose to $61.7M versus the year-ago quarter amid improved underwriting results and higher investment income.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $214.2M for Q2 2026, compared with $208.0M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 3.0%.
  • Net income was $61.7M attributable to common stockholders for Q2 2026, compared with $48.0M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 28.5%.
  • Diluted EPS was $2.05 for Q2 2026, compared with $1.55 in Q2 2025; YoY change 32.3%.

Business Highlights

  • Net premiums earned increased about 2.4% year over year, with total revenue aided by lower ceded premiums and stronger investment income.
  • Growth in personal residential premiums offset a pullback in commercial residential business amid competitive pressures in the Florida market.
  • Underwriting performance improved: the net combined ratio narrowed by 8 points to 64.9%, driven by favorable prior‑year reserve development and lower weather-related losses.
  • Reinsurance adjustments, including improved CAT XOL terms and a reduced quota-share ceded share, lowered the ceded premium ratio and supported retained premium growth.
  • Company continues to invest in data/AI analytics, selective underwriting, targeted geographic focus, and claims and customer-service enhancements to drive profitability.

Original SEC Filing: Heritage Insurance Holdings, Inc. [ HRTG ] - 10-Q - Aug. 07, 2026

data.title: Drilling Tools International Corp Q2 2026: Revenue $38.1M, EPS $(0.05) — 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Drilling Tools International Corp reported second-quarter 2026 results with revenue of $38.1M and a net loss attributable to common shareholders of $(1.79)M, or diluted EPS of $(0.05), an improvement versus the year-ago quarter.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue: $38.1M for Q2 2026, down from $39.4M in the year-ago quarter ( (3.4%)).
  • Net income: $(1.79)M attributable to common shareholders for Q2 2026, improved from $(2.41)M in the year-ago quarter.
  • Diluted EPS: $(0.05) for Q2 2026, versus $(0.07) in the year-ago quarter.

Business Highlights

  • Revenue mix: Tool rentals remain the primary revenue source at roughly 77–78% while product sales rose to about 22–23%, indicating growth in direct-tool sales.
  • Regional performance: Western Hemisphere revenue declined approximately 12–16% due to lower rental activity and pricing pressure; Eastern Hemisphere grew roughly 20–26% supported by acquisitions and expanded rental and product sales.
  • Operations: Longer laterals and improved drilling efficiency have partially offset reduced rig counts, supporting demand for select products and services.
  • Capital and recovery: Continued capital expenditures to maintain and expand the rental fleet, with rental tool recovery sales materially offsetting replacement spending.
  • Outlook and costs: Rising input and personnel costs are expected to pressure near-term margins; management says liquidity is sufficient for at least the next 12 months to support operations.

Original SEC Filing: Drilling Tools International Corp [ DTI ] - 10-Q - Aug. 07, 2026
